questions.q: What is the difference between a Matching Rule and a Duplicate Rule?
options: A Matching Rule decides what happens on a hit; a Duplicate Rule decides whether two records match
A Matching Rule decides whether two records match; a Duplicate Rule decides what happens on a hit
They are two names for the same configuration object
Matching Rules apply to Leads only; Duplicate Rules apply to Accounts and Contacts only
questions.explain: Matching Rules compare fields to decide if records are likely duplicates. Duplicate Rules point at a matching rule and decide the resulting action — block, alert, or report.

questions.q: Which standard matching/duplicate rule pairs ship active in a brand-new org?
options: All three pairs (Account, Contact, Lead) are active by default
Only the Account pair is active by default
None of them — all three pairs exist but must be activated manually
Only the matching rules are active; the duplicate rules still need activation
questions.explain: The three standard pairs exist in every org but ship inactive. Both the matching rule and its duplicate rule must be activated before anything fires.

questions.q: A duplicate rule is set to Block on Create. What does the user experience when they try to save a likely duplicate?
options: The save is rejected outright and the configured Alert Text is shown
The record saves and a report is generated for later review
The record saves with a warning banner the user can dismiss
Nothing — Block only affects edits, not new records
questions.explain: Block rejects the save entirely and displays the rule's Alert Text, forcing the user to change the data or use the existing record.

questions.q: Why might an admin choose Allow + Report instead of Block for a Lead duplicate rule?
options: Report is required before Block can ever be configured
Report rules run faster than Block rules
Allow + Report disables the matching rule entirely
It lets reps keep working without interruption while still giving admins a log to review
questions.explain: Allow + Report saves the record silently and logs the match to a Duplicate Record Set, giving visibility without slowing down a rep's workflow — useful where false positives are more likely.

questions.q: You built a correct custom duplicate rule, but it still isn't catching anything in testing. What's the most likely cause?
options: Custom duplicate rules are not supported on the Contact object
The rule, its linked matching rule, or both are still inactive
Duplicate rules only run during nightly batch jobs, not real-time saves
Alert Text was left blank, which disables the rule
questions.explain: A rule does nothing until both the matching rule and the duplicate rule that references it are activated — a common thing to forget after building one.
